brief.headline: Semis surge in neutral tape; gold and energy retreat
brief.regime_summary: SPY sits 1.5% above its 50-day and 7.9% above its 200-day, up 1.3% on the week, but the tape is not broadly healthy. Only 36% of sectors hold above their 50-day MAs. Eight of eleven sectors show negative 20-day momentum, with only Technology (XLK +4.2%) and Communication Services (XLC +1.7%) in positive territory. VIX at 16.28 is modestly above its 20-day average of 15.74, suggesting contained but not complacent anxiety. This is a narrow, tech-led tape: leadership is concentrated and fragile if that cluster rolls.

portfolio.note: Up 4.5% this week, sitting 3.2% above the 20-day MA and 3.9% below the 20-day high at RSI 63. Earnings on Oct 28 are the next catalyst; ATR is 2.3% so a one-ATR pullback would test the 20-day.

Earnings on Oct 14 are 16 days away. Stock is 3.4% above the 20-day but 2.6% off its 20-day high with a mixed DMA stack; at P/E 60.2 (53% premium to history), any guidance miss will be punished. Watch the 20-day MA at roughly 1685 as the key hold level.

Down 3.0% this week; now 2.6% below its 20-day MA and 5.7% off the 20-day high with RSI at 45.9. Cost basis is 88 versus current price of 62.04, a 29.5% loss. Sector 20-day momentum in XLE is nearly flat (+0.2%) while crude sits close to its 20-day MA; watch whether WTI holds 95 to stabilize the position.

GLD fell 1.9% this week and is now 1.5% below its 20-day MA, 7.4% off the 20-day high, with 20-day momentum at -6.9% and RSI 45.2. The DMA stack has flipped mixed and the score is -0.28. The thesis, holding gold as a risk hedge, deserves a review given that the broad risk-off metals complex (gold, silver) is selling off together.

watchlist.name: Meta Platforms, Inc.
watchlist.thesis: META gained 13.0% this week and sits 13.8% above its 20-day MA with RSI at 71.4. Revenue is estimated to grow 26.5% this year; 20-day relative strength versus the market is +31.4%. Earnings on Oct 28 are a hard catalyst. In a narrow tech-led tape this is the clearest leader, but it is extended.
watchlist.risk: RSI above 71 and 13.8% stretch above the 20-day mean any fade in risk appetite accelerates a reversion; 45 of 49 analyst revisions in the past 30 days went lower.

watchlist.name: QUALCOMM Incorporated
watchlist.thesis: QCOM surged 13.7% this week and is 11.6% above its 20-day MA at 180.97 with RSI 68. 20-day and 40-day RS versus the market are both above 20%. Forward P/E of 19.8 is 8.9% below its historical median, giving some fundamental cushion. Stock is only 1.9% below the 20-day high of 205.85.
watchlist.risk: EPS estimates for this fiscal year are actually declining (-12.9%), with 27 of 28 estimate revisions trending down over the last 30 days; the move is momentum-driven, not estimate-driven.

watchlist.name: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.
watchlist.thesis: AMD up 12.7% this week, 19.4% above the 20-day MA, RSI 73.0. EPS estimates revised up 28 times vs 9 down in the last 30 days, with CY EPS growth of 81.7%. At trailing P/E 161 it is 60% rich to its own history, but forward P/E of 40.5 and a $50.9B revenue estimate for the year provide the growth anchor.
watchlist.risk: The trailing multiple is 161x; any deceleration in AI-related data-center orders ahead of the Nov 3 earnings would collapse the setup quickly.

watchlist.name: Intel Corporation
watchlist.thesis: INTC up 13.3% this week, 17.7% above the 20-day MA, RSI 66.9. The 20-day RS versus market is +33.3%, the strongest in the screen. ATR of 5.1% is the widest on this list, reflecting still-elevated stock-specific risk into Oct 22 earnings.
watchlist.risk: EPS revisions are flat with zero ups and zero downs; the move appears sentiment rather than estimate driven, and the large ATR means whipsaw risk is high into earnings.

watchlist.name: Adobe Inc.
watchlist.thesis: ADBE fell 5.4% this week and is 9.3% below its 20-day MA with RSI at 36.6. It is 20.1% below the 20-day high, and 20-day momentum is -18.6%. Trailing P/E of 13.1 is 56.9% below its historical median, but the market is not rewarding the cheapness yet. RS versus the sector over 20 and 40 days is deeply negative (-22.8% and -16.8%).
watchlist.risk: A reversal in the broader tech selloff or a positive preannouncement before Dec 9 earnings could squeeze a low-RSI, high-short-interest name sharply.

watchlist.name: Novo Nordisk A/S
watchlist.thesis: NVO dropped 10.3% this week, sits in a full bearish DMA stack, and is 10.0% below its 20-day MA with RSI 31.2. EPS estimates have been cut (-2.1% revision), and trailing P/E of 9.7 looks optically cheap but is tagged as rich versus history (pe_vs_hist of +2.46). News flow centers on pipeline diversification, signaling core GLP-1 franchise pressure.
watchlist.risk: RSI at 31.2 is approaching oversold; a pipeline readout or favorable regulatory news this week (pharma-heavy calendar) could produce a sharp relief bounce.

commodities.name: WTI crude
commodities.note: WTI at 95.68 is flat on the week (-0.1%) and sitting just 0.25% below its 20-day MA. Bullish DMA stack intact with 20-day momentum at +14.7%, but RSI at 54 and 10.4% below the 20-day high suggest the recent rally is pausing. Watch the 20-day MA as support.

commodities.name: Gold
commodities.note: Gold fell 4.6% this week to 4182, now 4.7% below the 20-day MA and 8.3% off the 20-day high with RSI 33.6 approaching oversold. DMA stack has turned mixed; a break below recent lows would shift it to bearish. GLD in the portfolio mirrors this weakness.

commodities.name: Natural gas
commodities.note: Nat gas surged 10.4% this week to 3.132 and is 6.1% above its 20-day MA with RSI 60.5. Momentum is positive at both 20- and 40-day horizons (+8.5% and +14.0%). Thin liquidity tag warrants caution on any rapid reversal.

commodities.name: Silver
commodities.note: Silver dropped 6.3% this week and now sits in a bearish DMA stack, 5.2% below the 20-day MA. Relative volume of 17.4x is anomalous, possibly a position liquidation event. Watch whether the selling extends or exhausts near current levels.

commodities.name: Copper
commodities.note: Copper at 6.64 is holding just above its 20-day MA (+0.8%) with RSI 52.8 and modest 20-day momentum of +1.2%. Relative volume is elevated at 8.8x. As a cyclical read, copper's sideways behavior is consistent with the neutral-to-cautious macro regime.

risks: Narrow leadership: only XLK and XLC show positive 20-day momentum. If semiconductors fade after a 12-14% weekly surge in QCOM, AMD, INTC, the index has little else to hold it.
ASML earnings on Oct 14 and MSFT/META earnings on Oct 28 arrive with stocks extended; any guidance cut into a still-elevated valuation environment could spread sector contagion.
Gold and silver are both breaking down simultaneously, suggesting possible broad risk-off or dollar-strength event that could also pressure equities if it accelerates.

Only 36% of sectors are above their 50-day MAs. Breadth is thin; the market cap-weighted index masks significant underlying deterioration in Industrials (XLI -4.4%), Financials (XLF -4.9%), Real Estate (XLRE -6.2%) and Utilities (XLU -7.8%).
NVO's 10% single-week drop and ongoing GLP-1 franchise concerns could spread to the broader healthcare/biotech complex if clinical readouts this week disappoint.
